title: SpeedHire triage slate and evidence mapping (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines a condensed hiring and onboarding flow we call SpeedHire — for reactive, high-priority IC and IC+ roles where time-to-embed matters more than formal process cleanliness. It pairs a triage slate (prioritized evidence requirements), a lightweight interview stress-test rubric, and a 10-day rapid-embed checklist that minimizes ramp friction while preserving quality signals.

When to use SpeedHire:
- Role is mission-critical and needs headcount in 3–6 weeks (e.g., outage response, revenue retention spike, critical infra bugfix).
- Candidate pool is limited (internal referrals + outbound) and we must accept slightly higher hiring risk with mitigations.
- Hiring manager commits to an accelerated onboarding bundle (buddy allocation, focused eval tasks, prioritized access).

High-level principles:
1) Evidence-first, not schedule-first: Define the minimum evidence needed to make a hire decision before scheduling.
2) Conservative embedding: If we accelerate hiring, we add post-hire checkpoints to catch regressions.
3) Transparent tradeoffs: Hiring manager signs off on quality tradeoffs, budget for extra mentor time and paired work.

Triage slate (what we require per role tier):
- Tier A (Safety/Revenue critical): 3 evidence buckets required: live system debugging exercise OR replay session, paired problem solving session, at least one concrete prior impact (doc/link).
- Tier B (Core infra / product features): 2 evidence buckets required: take-home micro-project (3–6 hours) OR live coupled coding + spec review, and behavioral probe linked to cross-team collaboration.
- Tier C (supporting roles / short-term projects): 1 evidence bucket required: structured interview + reference check.

Evidence mapping matrix (example entries):
- "Live system debugging" -> demonstrates triage process, ownership, communication under pressure. Target artifacts: call transcript, terminal logs, one-paragraph write-up.
- "Paired problem session" -> shows collaborative coding, PR review behavior. Target artifacts: recording/notes, rubric score.
- "Prior impact doc" -> short case study (1 page) with success metrics and role description.

Interview stress-test rubric (scoring 1–4; pass threshold depends on tier):
- Technical correctness (1–4): ability to propose and validate a fix or design.
- Signal prioritization (1–4): chooses reasonable diagnostics and a mitigation path.
- Communication under pressure (1–4): clear, calm explanations and next steps.
- Ownership intent (1–4): articulates follow-up and monitoring plan.
- Collaboration (1–4): invites others, uses feedback, escalates appropriately.

Quick scoring guidance:
- Tier A pass: >=14/20 and no subscore <3 on Technical or Ownership.
- Tier B pass: >=11/20 with no subscore <2 on Technical.
- Tier C pass: >=8/20.

Decision window & cooling-off protocol:
- Decision window: 48 hours from final interview to offer or rejection. Recruiter drafts feedback, hiring manager signs.
- Cooling-off: If score falls within +/-1 of threshold, schedule a 60-minute follow-up pairing task (not a full loop) within 5 business days.

Reference checks (targeted, not wholesale):
- Ask for one reference focused on the primary risk (e.g., incident response, product delivery).
- Use a 6-question template emphasizing timeline, collaboration, and failure mode.

Offer packaging for SpeedHire:
- Standard comp band + 2-week discretionary ramp stipend (covers training, travel, home office).
- 30/60/90 success milestones defined in offer pack to align expectations.

10-day rapid-embed onboarding checklist (post-accept):
Day 0 (pre-join): hardware order confirmed, access list created, first-week schedule with buddy assigned.
Day 1: orientation + intro to team roadmap (30m), systems onboarding (1 hr), buddy pairing (2 hrs: shadow + tiny task).
Day 2–3: paired work on an existing low-risk ticket with mentor; ship a small commit and review.
Day 4–7: rotate through 1) oncall runbook read, 2) core infra crash course (recorded sessions), 3) join two cross-team syncs as observer.
Day 8–10: independent ownership of a scoped bug/feature with mentor review; 1:1 with manager to align 30/60/90 goals.

Post-hire checkpoints (mitigations for accelerated risk):
- Week 2: Technical review + buddy feedback (structured notes).
- Week 4: Quality gate: candidate must have shipped or produced an approved design doc; otherwise transition to mentoring plan.
- Week 8: Bar-raise evaluation: hiring manager + eng lead sign-off on continued role fit or consider role adjustments.

Hiring noise reduction (practical tips):
- Standardize the take-home tasks and rubric per role family. Keep tasks time-boxed at 3–6 hours.
- Use the same 1-page scorecard template across interviews to simplify decisions.
- Automate post-offer paperwork and access tickets to avoid first-week delays.

Operational checklist for recruiters: 
- Confirm role tier and triage slate with hiring manager before sourcing.
- Share candidate evidence checklist at time of panel scheduling.
- Collect artifacts (links, short write-ups) and attach to candidate card.
- Ensure one-person assigned to track post-hire checkpoints.

Templates appended (copy-paste friendly):
- 1-page Scorecard header: role, tier, date, interviewers, artifacts attached, final numeric total, hire/no-hire/recheck.
- Reference check script: 6 questions + red-flag indicators.
- Offer milestone bullet list for 30/60/90.

Open questions & next steps (WIP):
- Do we standardize SpeedHire for all teams or leave to hiring manager discretion? (action: product + infra leads to align).
- Should we create a small pool of on-call mentors funded by recruiting ops for SpeedHire hires? (action: people-ops to cost out).
- Pilot metrics: time-to-hire, first-30-day PR velocity, manager satisfaction. Run a 6-month pilot with 12 hires and report.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and operational; please flag any legal/compensation redlines.
- I pulled the reference script from CONFLUENCE-12345 and condensed it — need people-ops canonical link.
